section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the impact of goal difficulty and specificity on individual and group performance, noting that specific and difficult goals generally lead to higher performance, especially in well-learned and low-complexity tasks. It reviews research on group-level goals, including a study by Weingart and Weldon (1991) and a multilevel theory by DeShon et al. (2004), which suggests that goals function similarly at individual and team levels. The section concludes by proposing that difficult team goals may hinder adaptation to changing task contexts.
